story.title: Country Emoji Quiz
story.midCtaText: Enjoying the quiz? Subscribe & hit the bell!
story.subscribeText: New quiz every day – turn on the bell 🔔

questions.fact: Lady Liberty was dedicated in New York Harbor in 1886.
Wild giant pandas live only in the mountains of China.
The Great Pyramid was the tallest building for about 3,800 years.
Mexico City stands on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan.
Big Ben is the name of the bell – not the clock tower.
Venice is built on more than 100 small islands.
BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen are all German.
Russia stretches across 11 time zones.
Paella comes from Valencia on Spain's east coast.
India makes more films each year than any other country.
The first Olympic Games were held at Olympia in 776 BC.
Ireland's official emblem is the harp, not the shamrock.
New Zealand still has about 4.5 sheep for every person.
Belgians say they invented fries – not the French.
Muay Thai is called the art of eight limbs.
Tango was born in Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the 1800s.
Iceland sits right on the line where two tectonic plates meet.
K-pop band BTS formed in Seoul in 2010.
The Barcelos rooster is a famous symbol of Portugal.
Norway's coast has more than 1,000 fjords.
Finland has about three million saunas.
Usain Bolt and Bob Marley are both from Jamaica.
Mongolia is the least densely populated country on Earth.
Mozart was born in Salzburg in 1756.
Wild lemurs are native only to Madagascar.
LEGO comes from Denmark – the name means "play well".
Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia is the world's largest salt flat.
Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through it.
Easter Island and its famous moai statues belong to Chile.
The word "cravat" comes from "Croat" – the tie's origin.

lines.q: Thirty countries in emojis, from easy to legend, and they get harder every round. Keep score! First one: a statue, a burger, and an eagle.
lines.a: The USA! Lady Liberty has watched over New York since eighteen eighty six.

lines.q: A panda, chopsticks, and a red lantern.
lines.a: China! Wild pandas live nowhere else.

lines.q: A camel, a pyramid, and an ancient urn.
lines.a: Egypt! The Great Pyramid held the height record for about three thousand eight hundred years.

lines.q: A taco, a cactus, and a piñata.
lines.a: Mexico! The capital sits right on top of the old Aztec city.

lines.q: A royal guard, a teapot, and a big red bus.
lines.a: The United Kingdom! Fun fact, Big Ben is actually the bell, not the tower.

lines.q: Pasta, a gondola, and a carnival mask.
lines.a: Italy! Venice is built on over a hundred little islands. Six out of six so far? Nice start.

lines.q: Round two, medium. A pretzel, a beer, and a car.
lines.a: Germany! Home of BMW, Mercedes and Volkswagen.

lines.q: A nesting doll, ballet shoes, and a bear.
lines.a: Russia! It stretches across eleven time zones.

lines.q: A pan of paella, a flamenco dancer, and a bull.
lines.a: Spain! Paella was born in Valencia.

lines.q: Curry, a cricket bat, and a movie clapper.
lines.a: India! It makes more films than anywhere else on Earth.

lines.q: Ancient columns, olives, and a painted vase.
lines.a: Greece! The very first Olympics were held there in seven seventy six BC.

lines.q: A clover, a pint, and a fiddle.
lines.a: Ireland! Plot twist, the official symbol is actually the harp. Still with me? Good.

lines.q: Round three, hard. A kiwi, a sheep, and a rugby ball.
lines.a: New Zealand! There are still about four and a half sheep per person.

lines.q: Chocolate, waffles, and fries.
lines.a: Belgium! And Belgians will tell you fries were never French.

lines.q: A temple, a coconut, and a boxing glove.
lines.a: Thailand! Muay Thai is the art of eight limbs. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: A mate cup, a steak, and a tango dancer.
lines.a: Argentina! Tango grew up on the streets of Buenos Aires.

lines.q: A volcano, hot springs, and a whale.
lines.a: Iceland! The whole island sits where two tectonic plates pull apart.

lines.q: A microphone, cabbage, and a smartphone.
lines.a: South Korea! K-pop, kimchi, and Samsung. Halfway done? You're doing great.

lines.q: Round four, very hard. A rooster, a football, and a fish.
lines.a: Portugal! The lucky Barcelos rooster, football, and lots of cod.

lines.q: A troll, a salmon, and skis.
lines.a: Norway! Trolls, salmon, and more than a thousand fjords.

lines.q: A sauna, Santa Claus, and a mobile phone.
lines.a: Finland! Saunas, Santa's home in Lapland, and Nokia. About three million saunas, by the way.

lines.q: A sprinter, music, and a palm tree.
lines.a: Jamaica! Usain Bolt and Bob Marley, same island.

lines.q: A horse, a round tent, and an eagle.
lines.a: Mongolia! The emptiest country on the planet.

lines.q: A violin, skis, and a slice of chocolate cake.
lines.a: Austria! Mozart, the Alps, and Sachertorte. Still standing? Respect.

lines.q: Final round, legend. A monkey-like animal, a fat tree, and an island.
lines.a: Madagascar! Lemurs and baobab trees.

lines.q: Toy bricks, a mermaid, and a bicycle.
lines.a: Denmark! LEGO means play well, and the Little Mermaid sits in Copenhagen.

lines.q: Salt, a llama, and a mountain.
lines.a: Bolivia! Home of the biggest salt flat in the world. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: A giant tortoise, a globe line, and roses.
lines.a: Ecuador! Named after the equator, and the Galápagos belong to it.

lines.q: A stone head, a chili, and wine.
lines.a: Chile! Easter Island is part of Chile, thousands of kilometres offshore.

lines.q: Final question. A spotty dog, a necktie, and a beach.
lines.a: Croatia! Dalmatians come from Dalmatia, and the necktie started as the Croatian cravat.
